title.zh: 同一个想法，两份手稿：1858年林奈学会的一次安排
title.en: One Idea, Two Manuscripts: An Arrangement at the Linnean Society, 1858

dek.zh: 华莱士从马来群岛寄来一篇论文；莱尔和胡克认为，它与达尔文多年未发表的手稿讲的是同一套理论。两人决定把双方的材料同场宣读，并把理由写成一封信。
dek.en: Wallace sends a paper from the Malay Archipelago; Lyell and Hooker judge that it sets out the same theory as a manuscript Darwin has left unpublished for years. They arrange for both men's material to be read together, and set down their reasons in a letter.

heading.zh: 一封信，三份材料，一个不好开口的问题
heading.en: One Letter, Three Packets, and a Question Hard to Ask

paras.zh: 1858年6月30日，伦敦。两位皇家学会会员莱尔与胡克联名给林奈学会秘书贝内特写信，随信附上几份材料；信里说，这些材料都关于同一个主题。麻烦在于：同一套理论被两个人各自独立想了出来，而两个人都没把它发表出去。信里称二人“可公平地声称是这一重要的研究方向上的原创思想者”。
paras.en: London, 30 June 1858. Charles Lyell and Joseph Dalton Hooker, both Fellows of the Royal Society, wrote a joint letter to J. J. Bennett, secretary of the Linnean Society, enclosing papers which, they said, "all relate to the same subject". The difficulty was: the same theory had occurred to two men working independently of each other, and neither had published. Both men, the letter says, "may both fairly claim the merit of being original thinkers in this important line of inquiry."

heading.en: Two Men Who Never Compared Notes

paras.zh: 先把两位当事人摆出来。达尔文这边，有一份关于物种的手稿：1839年草拟，1844年誊写，胡克在1844年读过誊本，内容后来又告诉了莱尔。多年里，莱尔和胡克反复催达尔文把观点发表出来，他一直没有。华莱士这边，1854年出发去东印度，在马来群岛一带考察了近八年，研究这些岛屿和部分巴布亚的动植物；更早的1848年，他与贝茨同赴巴西，走亚马逊和内格罗河的原始森林，1852年返英，他那批尤以鸟类和植物见长的收藏，大半毁于海难。1877年的一篇人物小传记下关键的一句：他在马来群岛研究时并不知道达尔文在同一方向上的先前工作，却得出了几乎相同的结论。
paras.en: Begin with the two men themselves. Darwin had a manuscript on species: drafted in 1839, copied out in 1844. Hooker read that copy in 1844, and its contents later reached Lyell. For years the two of them pressed Darwin to publish his views; for years he held back. Wallace, meanwhile, was travelling. He set out for the East Indies in 1854 and spent nearly eight years exploring the islands of the Malay Archipelago and parts of Papua, studying their animals and plants. Earlier, in 1848, he had gone to Brazil with Bates, through the primeval forests of the Amazon and the Rio Negro, and returned to England in 1852; the collections he brought home, especially rich in birds and plants, were largely destroyed by shipwreck. A sketch published in 1877 supplies the decisive sentence: while pursuing his researches in the Malay Archipelago, Wallace was unaware of Darwin's earlier labours in the same direction, yet arrived at almost the same general conclusions.

paras.zh: 于是问题不是谁对，而是两个人各自独立做出同一件事时，功劳怎么分、由谁来分。一种解释是，这件事必须落到纸面上：谁署名、谁先讲、由哪个机构讲、按什么顺序讲。莱尔和胡克选择由自己出面安排，并把理由写进一封公开发表的信里。
paras.en: So the question was never who was right. It was what to do when two people have independently done the same thing: how credit gets divided, and who divides it. On one reading, it had to be settled on paper - whose name went on the work, who spoke first, through which institution, and in what order. Lyell and Hooker chose to arrange the matter themselves, and to write their reasoning into a letter made for publication.

heading.en: Where the Three Items Came From

paras.zh: 达尔文的那份旧手稿有点尴尬：它从未打算发表。1858年，达尔文为这份手稿加了一条脚注，署“C. D. 1858”：这份手稿从未打算发表，因此写得并不仔细。
paras.en: Darwin's old manuscript was awkward in a particular way: it was never intended for publication. In 1858 he added a footnote to it: "This MS. work was never intended for publication, and therefore was not written with care.—C. D. 1858.".

paras.zh: 为了显示他的看法多年没有改变，莱尔和胡克选了第二份材料：达尔文1857年10月写给美国波士顿的阿萨·格雷教授的一封私人信的摘要，信中重申了他的看法，表明这些看法从1839年到1857年没有改变。
paras.en: To show that his views had not changed over the years, Lyell and Hooker chose a second item: an abstract of a private letter Darwin had written in October 1857 to Professor Asa Gray, of Boston, in which he repeated his views, and which showed that they had remained unaltered from 1839 to 1857.

paras.zh: 这里有一处材料对不上，照实说：莱尔和胡克的信把这封信写作1857年10月，而这份摘要自己的标题写的是1857年9月5日于唐恩。两说并存，证据里没有更多材料可以判谁对，本文也不替它们裁决。
paras.en: One detail does not match, and is best reported as it stands. Lyell and Hooker's letter dates this letter October 1857, while the abstract's own heading gives 5 September 1857, at Down. Both datings stand in the record; nothing further in the evidence decides between them, and this article does not settle it.

paras.zh: 第三份材料是华莱士的论文，标题《论变种无限偏离原初类型的倾向》，落款特尔纳特，1858年2月。它是写给朋友兼通信者达尔文看的，作者表示：如果达尔文认为它足够新颖、有意思，就请转给莱尔。三份材料开头的风格各不相同。达尔文的摘录从德堪多讲起：德堪多曾雄辩地宣称，整个自然都处在战争之中，生物与生物相争，或与外部自然相争；接着说，这就是马尔萨斯的学说，而且多数情形下作用强了十倍。华莱士则从一条反对意见讲起：家养变种不稳定，任其自然便常常回到亲本的样子，有人以此认为物种是分别创造、永远不变的。出发点不同，落点接近。
paras.en: The third item was Wallace's essay, "On the Tendency of Varieties to depart indefinitely from the Original Type," dated Ternate, February 1858. It was written for his friend and correspondent Darwin to read, with the express wish that, "if Mr. Darwin thought it sufficiently novel and interesting," it should be forwarded to Lyell. The openings read very differently. Darwin's extract opens from De Candolle and Malthus: "De Candolle, in an eloquent passage, has declared that all nature is at war, one organism with another, or with external nature.", and its next breath calls the struggle "the doctrine of Malthus applied in most cases with tenfold force." Wallace opens from an objection - that domestic varieties are unstable and tend to revert to the parent form, which is taken to show that species were created distinct and are kept that way. Different starting points, converging destinations.

paras.zh: 达尔文收到论文后的做法，莱尔和胡克写得很具体：他写信给莱尔，提议征得华莱士本人同意后，尽快把这篇论文发表。两位中间人表示赞成，但附了一个条件：达尔文不能像他（为照顾华莱士）“强烈倾向”的那样，扣下自己关于同一主题的手稿。信里记下的是达尔文的倾向：把发表的机会让给对方。
paras.en: What Darwin did on receiving the essay, Lyell and Hooker describe precisely. He wrote to Lyell proposing to obtain Wallace's consent and have the essay published as soon as possible. The two intermediaries approved - with one condition: that Darwin must not withhold his own memoir on the same subject, "as he was strongly inclined to do (in favour of Mr. Wallace)". The letter records his inclination: to stand aside and leave the field to the other man.

paras.zh: 莱尔和胡克向达尔文说明了这样做的理由，达尔文同意由他们自行处置他的手稿。他们写下的理由不止是替两人分先后：他们说，这样做不只是考虑他与他的朋友谁更有优先权，而是为了科学的整体利益。他们又补了一句实在话：科学界正等着达尔文的完整著作，与其空等，不如先把他多年劳作的一些主要结果，连同那位能干的通信者的结果，一起摆到公众面前，让别人立刻有一个可以出发的目标。
paras.en: Lyell and Hooker put their reasoning to Darwin, and he gave them permission to make what use they thought proper of his memoir. Their grounds went beyond ranking two men: "we are not solely considering the relative claims to priority of himself and his friend, but the interests of science generally". Then a plain practical point. The scientific world was waiting for Darwin's complete work; better that some of the leading results of his years of labour should be laid before the public now, together with those of his able correspondent, and at once constitute "a goal from which others may start."

paras.zh: 1858年7月1日，林奈学会宣读了这批材料。信中把三份材料按日期排列：1839年草拟、1844年誊写的手稿摘录，1857年致格雷信的摘要，华莱士1858年2月的论文；当天按什么顺序宣读，材料没有记。十九年后那篇小传的记述是：华莱士的论文经莱尔转交林奈学会，1858年7月1日宣读，与达尔文的论文同场；小传给出的标题是《论物种形成变种的倾向，以及物种与变种借自然选择得以延续》。
paras.en: On 1 July 1858 the material was read to the Linnean Society. The letter lists the three items by date: extracts from the manuscript drafted in 1839 and copied in 1844, the abstract of the 1857 letter to Gray, and Wallace's essay of February 1858; the order in which they were read that day is not recorded. Nineteen years later the sketch of Wallace recorded that his essay, transmitted through Sir Charles Lyell to the Linnean Society, "was read before that body on July 1, 1858, coincidently with the reading of Mr, Darwin's paper" - the sketch gives the title as "On the Tendency of Species to form Varieties, and on the Perpetuation of Species and Varieties by means of Natural Selection".

paras.zh: 小传还顺笔记下华莱士后来的路：1862年回英国，此后多年整理他庞大的收藏——十万余件昆虫标本、八千多只鸟；1868年获皇家学会奖章，1870年获巴黎地理学会金质奖章，同年出版《自然选择理论文集》。而在人类起源问题上，他不接受达尔文的结论，认为单靠自然选择不足以完成从类人猿到人的过渡，还需某种更高原因的共同作用。作者的看法：被放在共同发现者位置上的人，后来并没有因此变成附议者。
paras.en: The sketch also follows Wallace's later course. He returned to England in 1862 and spent several years classifying an enormous collection - upward of 100,000 insect specimens and more than 8,000 birds. In 1868 the Royal Society gave him its royal medal; in 1870 the Geographical Society of Paris its gold medal, and in that same year he published "Contributions to the Theory of Natural Selection". On human origins he still would not follow Darwin: natural selection alone, he held, was not competent to effect the transition from the anthropoid apes to man without the joint agency of some higher cause. The author's view: the man placed in the position of co-discoverer did not become a follower because of it.

paras.zh: 一种解释是：莱尔和胡克这套安排，实质上是把功劳归属从两个人之间的争议，改写成一个程序问题。他们能拿得出手的依据有三样：此前未公开的文本、可查的日期、两位中间人的说明。达尔文的旧手稿和致格雷的信摘要显示他想得早；华莱士的论文、落款与寄送方式，与莱尔和胡克关于两人互不知情的说法相符，而且论文由华莱士本人寄给达尔文，并请达尔文若认为它足够新颖、有意思，就转给莱尔。作者推断，他们之所以特意强调两人互不知情、且都没发表，正是因为在谁先想到之外，还有一个更难回答的问题：想到而不发表，算不算占住了位置。
paras.en: One reading of the arrangement is this: Lyell and Hooker rewrote a dispute between two men over credit as a question of procedure. What they could put on the table was of three kinds - texts not previously published, dates that could be checked, and the account of two intermediaries. Darwin's old manuscript and the abstract of the Gray letter showed how early he had reached the idea; Wallace's essay, with its dateline and the manner of its sending, was consistent with Lyell and Hooker's statement that the two men had worked unknown to one another, and it was Wallace himself who had sent the essay to Darwin, with the express wish that Darwin forward it to Lyell if he thought it sufficiently novel and interesting. The author's inference: they stressed so heavily that the two men did not know of each other's work and that neither had published, because beyond who thought of it first there sits a harder question - whether thinking of something and never publishing is enough to hold your place.

paras.zh: 作者把他们的做法概括为：算，但要公开兑现。作者提出的替代做法至少有三种，各有代价：由达尔文先单独发表；只发华莱士，把达尔文的优先权留给他日后自述；或者都等达尔文的完整著作出来再说。列在这里作对照的是作者提出的选项，不是材料里的记载。实际被选中的是第四条：三份材料同场宣读，日期写进正文，理由写给一位秘书并公开发表。莱尔和胡克自己说，这样做的依据是让经年思考、建立在大量事实上的观点立刻成为别人可以出发的目标。分配交给了程序，当事人的让步只是其中一步。
paras.en: The author's summary of their course is: yes, but it has to be cashed in publicly. The author sets out at least three alternative courses, each with its own price: Darwin publishing alone first; only Wallace published, with Darwin left to state his own priority later; or everyone waiting for Darwin's complete book. What is listed here for contrast are options constructed by the author, not episodes recorded in the documents. The course actually taken was a fourth: three sets of material read together in one session, the dates printed in the body of the text, the reasoning addressed to a secretary and made public. The warrant Lyell and Hooker gave was that views founded on a wide deduction from facts and matured by years of reflection should at once become a goal from which others might start. The allocation was handed to a procedure; a party's willingness to give way was one step in it, not the deciding one.

paras.zh: 现代虚构场景一：一位研究员的一篇方法草稿在硬盘里放了三年，同事一再催她投出去，她总觉得还不够好。某天，她在预印本网站上看到别人刚发了几乎一样的方法。这时候能拿出来的，只有草稿的版本记录，以及那几位早年读过草稿的同事愿不愿意写下他们看到过什么。
paras.en: Fictional modern scene one. A researcher has kept a draft of a method on her hard drive for three years; colleagues keep urging her to submit it, and she keeps feeling it is not ready. One day she finds almost the same method in a preprint someone has just posted. What she can produce now is the version history of her draft, and whether the colleagues who read it years ago are willing to put in writing what they saw.

paras.zh: 现代虚构场景二：一位中学老师把实验设计发在自己的公众号上，一位研究生几乎同时写成论文投稿。两人都不想争，编辑说他不能替他们判定谁算原创，只能请双方各交材料、写清时间线，再请一位双方都认的同行来安排刊出方式。
paras.en: A modern fictional scene, second. A secondary-school teacher puts an experimental design on her own public account, and a graduate student writes up nearly the same design and submits it almost at the same time. Neither wants a fight. The editor says he cannot pronounce on who counts as original. He can only ask both sides for their material and a clear timeline, then invite a peer both accept to arrange how the work appears in print.

heading.zh: 这份材料不能告诉我们什么
heading.en: What This Record Cannot Tell Us

paras.zh: 本文依据的记录有两类，都要打折看。一类是莱尔和胡克1858年6月30日给林奈学会秘书的说明信，他们是安排的当事人，也是作证人；另一类是1877年《大众科学月刊》上的一篇人物小传，动笔时距1858年已近二十年。手头没有达尔文、华莱士完整的私人通信，所以本文不写他们的心情，不写他们当场的反应，也不写两人私下如何商量。
paras.en: The records this article rests on fall into two classes, and both deserve a discount. One is the explanatory letter Lyell and Hooker wrote to the secretary of the Linnean Society on 30 June 1858; they were at once parties to the arrangement and witnesses to it. The other is a personal sketch in Popular Science Monthly from 1877, written nearly twenty years after the event. With no full private correspondence of Darwin's or Wallace's in hand, this article does not write about their feelings, their reactions at the time, or how the two of them settled matters between themselves.

paras.zh: 同样，证据包没有说明华莱士在宣读之前是否知情、是否同意，这一点本文不作任何陈述。致格雷信的日期两说并存，照原样保留。宣读当天的具体经过，以及达尔文完整著作的出版过程，不在本文范围内。可以确定的只有这次安排本身：三份材料、一位收信人、一个日期，以及写在信上的理由。
paras.en: Likewise, the evidence does not say whether Wallace knew of the reading beforehand or consented to it, and this article makes no statement either way. The date of the letter to Gray stands in two versions and is left as found. How the reading itself went on the day, and how Darwin's complete work was later published, lie outside the scope here. What can be fixed is the arrangement itself: three sets of material, one addressee, one date, and the reasons written into the letter.

scenario.zh: 作者提出的虚构情境：两位互不相识的解题者各自独立完成了同一个证明，各自只有自己电脑上的草稿时间记录，没有第三方能证明谁先想到。一家期刊愿意接收，但要求先定下署名方式。
scenario.en: A fictional scenario proposed by the author: two problem-solvers who have never met independently complete the same proof. Each has only the timestamped drafts on his own computer, and no third party can show who thought of it first. A journal is willing to accept the work, but wants the order of the names settled first.

question.zh: 当没有人能证明谁先想到时，你更愿意把分功劳的权力交给谁——交给时间记录、交给一位双方都信任的中间人，还是交给两个人自己协商？为什么？
question.en: When nobody can prove who thought of it first, who would you rather give the power to divide credit - timestamped records, an intermediary both sides trust, or the two people working it out between themselves? Why?

assumptions.zh: 假设两人确实互不知情；双方都愿意署名；期刊不接受轮流单发。
assumptions.en: Assume the two really were unaware of each other; that both are willing to sign; and that the journal will not take them one at a time on alternating terms.

steps.zh: 一，各自提交带时间记录的完整草稿；二，请一位与双方无利益关系的同行核对，只核时间与独立性，不评优劣；三，同场公开两份材料，正文写明各自的时间线；四，并列署名，把说明写进正文而非私下约定。
steps.en: First, each submits a complete draft with its timestamped record. Second, a colleague with no stake in either side checks the material - only the timing and the independence, not the merits. Third, both sets of material are presented publicly in one session, with each timeline stated in the body of the text. Fourth, the byline is joint, and the explanation is printed in the text rather than left to a private understanding.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的另一种做法：用抽签或轮流决定署名顺序，以程序的随机换取和平。代价是它不留下任何关于谁做了什么的记录。
alternative.en: One alternative the author proposes: settle the order of the names by lot or by turns, trading procedural randomness for peace. The price is that it leaves no record of who did what.

uncertainty_note.zh: 本文依据的记录有二：莱尔与胡克1858年6月30日致林奈学会秘书的说明信（两人均为安排当事人），以及1877年一篇杂志人物小传。没有达尔文、华莱士完整的私人通信，故不写其心情与反应；华莱士在宣读前是否知情或同意，材料未载，本文不作陈述；致格雷信日期两说并存（1857年10月／1857年9月5日），不作裁决；宣读当天的具体经过与达尔文完整著作的出版不在范围内。
uncertainty_note.en: This article rests on two records: Lyell and Hooker's explanatory letter of 30 June 1858 to the secretary of the Linnean Society (both were parties to the arrangement), and a magazine personal sketch of 1877. No full private correspondence of Darwin's or Wallace's is in hand, so their feelings and reactions are not described; whether Wallace knew of or consented to the reading beforehand is not recorded in the material and no statement is made; the date of the letter to Gray stands in two versions (October 1857 / 5 September 1857) and is not adjudicated; how the reading went on the day and the later publication of Darwin's complete work fall outside the scope.

preheader.zh: 两份互不知情的手稿、两位安排者，和一句“不只是谁先谁后”。
preheader.en: Two independent manuscripts, two arrangers, and a reason beyond priority.

sources.citation: Darwin and Wallace, 'On the Tendency of Species to form Varieties…', Journal of the Proceedings of the Linnean Society (1858), with the covering letter of Lyell and Hooker, Wikisource

what.zh: 开头就是莱尔和胡克的说明信，交代了为什么把两人的材料放在一起宣读。
what.en: Opens with Lyell and Hooker's letter explaining why the two were read together.

episode.action: joint reading of Darwin's and Wallace's papers at the Linnean Society arranged by Lyell and Hooker
spans: en:On the tendency of species to form varieties; and on the Perpetuation of Varieties and Species by Natural Means of Selection
